wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected outcome is the validity of the restored data itself, so there is no neighbouring object a check could authorise instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the restore path applies no normalising or adjusting step to the decoded values before they are used, so there is no later point at which the attacker value would change
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no name, spelling or identity parsing is involved; the values are plain integers, offsets and byte strings
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority, role or secret lookup that could fail open

traps.shape: the reported route, read as a boundary shape: an atom sub-pattern id equal to sub_patterns.len() is still outside the array, but the published check `len < max_id` and the natural `id > len` both accept it
traps.realistic_because: the published fix's own shape is `sub_patterns.len() < max_id`, and the synthetic unwrap_or(0) value means a naive `>=` rejects rule sets that have no atoms at all

traps.shape: pattern B: anchored sub-pattern ids are resolved through the same unchecked sub_patterns access while the pattern search scans, but the published check only walks the atoms
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; reason to dismiss: anchored patterns are a separate optimisation path that never touches the Aho-Corasick atoms the report and the published check reason about

traps.shape: pattern B: a chained sub-pattern's chained_to id is followed through unchecked sub_patterns access during chain verification, and the published check never looks inside the sub-pattern values
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; reason to dismiss: the id is nested inside an enum value and chains look like a neighbouring feature rather than one of the top-level id vectors

traps.shape: pattern A far site plus producer invariant: the UTF-8 promise of a text metadata literal is made only by the compiler, the deserializer never re-checks it, and the read accessor asserts it with an unchecked conversion; the published fix only turns that into a panic at read time instead of refusing the blob
traps.realistic_because: real upstream code; reason to dismiss: it is a read-only accessor in another module whose own comment says the string is surely valid UTF-8, and the published fix already touched it

traps.shape: pattern B: forward and backward regex code locations from the blob are used to slice the regex code in the Fast/Pike VMs without a bounds check; the published fix never looks at them
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; reason to dismiss: bytecode validity reads as a compiler invariant and the VM is a separate engine package

traps.shape: injected sibling: the per-pattern fast-scan bit vector is read through an unchecked index in the scan hot path; a blob whose table is shorter than the pattern count is accepted but the read lands outside it
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer-style hot-path micro-optimisation of an existing checked lookup, with the same 'the compiler sizes it' comment style as the other unchecked accesses; reason to dismiss: a derived performance cache, not compiled rule data

traps.shape: injected sibling and producer off the check's path: pattern bounds are stored in a dense vector read through an unchecked index, but only Compiler::build pads the vector to one entry per pattern and the deserializer never calls the producer, so a short table is accepted
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer-style dense-vector replacement for a hash map in a hot loop; reason to dismiss: a table of optional bounds looks naturally sparse, so a short table reads as normal and its density is only visible in the producer
